suggested_experiment_name: Pulsar timing and neutron star constraints on axion-neutron coupling
notes: This is a theoretical paper proposing how neutron star inspirals observed by Advanced LIGO could constrain axion parameter space through mediation of long-range forces between neutron stars. The paper does NOT present measured exclusion limits or sensitivity projections with explicit numerical (mass, coupling) data points. Instead, it discusses qualitative signatures (changes to gravitational waveforms, scalar Larmor radiation, repulsive forces preventing merger) that would appear if axions couple to neutron stars via finite-density effects. Figure 6 shows a constraint diagram in the (m_a, f_a) plane with various astrophysical bounds (SN1987A, BBN, superradiance, binary pulsars, Earth, Sun, white dwarfs, neutron stars), but these are existing constraints from other sources, not new limits from this work. The paper explicitly states 'Numerical work will be important in determining the details' and leaves detailed waveform analysis to future work. No extractable numerical exclusion limit data (mass-coupling pairs) is presented for a new measurement or concrete projection. The coupling type is inferred as AxionNeutron because the mechanism involves axion sourcing by neutron star nuclear matter (neutrons and protons at finite density), though the paper does not explicitly quote g_an values. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 6 shows multiple constraint regions on the axion parameter space (m_a vs g_an). The primary exclusion boundary traced is the PULSAR constraint (purple shaded region), which represents a conservative estimate from orbital decay measurements of binary pulsar systems. The x-axis is Log₁₀[m_a/eV] ranging from -20 to 0, corresponding to axion masses from 1e-20 eV to 1 eV. The y-axis is Log₁₀[g_an/F_a] ranging from -6 to -20. The pulsar constraint forms a roughly horizontal band around Log₁₀(g_an/F_a) ≈ -17 to -18 across the mass range. Other constraints shown include SN1987A (orange), BBN (dotted), Earth/Sun (red/blue), White Dwarf, Neutron Star, and QCD Axion lines, but the primary extraction focuses on the pulsar boundary as indicated in the figure caption. The exact location depends on the neutron star mass-radius relation [38]. Confidence is moderate (0.65) due to the complexity of reading precise boundary values from the multi-constraint plot and the need to distinguish the pulsar region from overlapping constraints. | convention: AxionNeutron C_N/F_a [eV^-1] -> dimensionless g_aN (x1.879e+09) | Calibration: No calibration needed
